name: Ohio
$methodComment: GENUINELY DIFFERENT from PA/MI's flat_rate method and even from federal's annualize-then-bracket-then-deannualize approach. Ohio's own published method applies a PER-PERIOD exemption subtraction directly to the per-period wage, then looks up PER-PERIOD brackets (not annual brackets divided down) — see periodTables below, transcribed exactly from Ohio's own PDF rather than derived, because period counts (52/26/24/12/260) don't divide evenly and re-deriving from an annual figure risks an off-by-a-cent error in some frequencies that Ohio's own tables don't have. STALE NOTE REMOVED 2026-09-09: this comment used to say the engine had no dispatch case for 'bracket_per_period' and that Ohio could not be run through calculatePaycheck() at all. That was fixed some time ago — src/taxes/state.ts dispatches 'bracket_per_period' straight to ohioWithholding(), proven by tests/engine.test.ts's own Ohio suite — and this file's OWN knownGaps list already said so ('CLOSED: ohioWithholding() now implements the bracket_per_period method'). This top-of-file comment simply never got updated to match, so a reader hitting this comment first would have been told the opposite of what the rest of the file says. Caught during a source-accuracy audit that re-verified this file's withholding tables against Ohio's own PDF (byte-for-byte match) but also read the file end to end rather than stopping at the first comment.

sources.title: Employer Withholding Taxes - Percentage Method (Effective August 1, 2026)

sources.title: ODT updates employer withholding rates beginning August 1, 2026 (Ohio Society of CPAs summary of House Bill 96, 136th General Assembly)
sources.note: Context for WHY the table changed mid-year: HB96 reduced Ohio income tax rates, effective for payroll periods ENDING on or after 2026-08-01. As of this project's stated as-of date (2026-08-11), the August 1 table is the one currently in force — an earlier (pre-Aug-1) table would be wrong for a check dated today despite both being '2026' tables. This mid-year effective-dating split is a real gotcha unique to Ohio among the jurisdictions modelled so far.

sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and text-extracted directly. CLOSES the previously-disclosed gap: this table was still in force for Ohio payroll periods ending in January-July 2026, before HB96's August 1 change — see priorTable2026 below.

sources.title: Ohio Revised Code Section 5747.06(A) -- Withholding exemptions, paragraphs (1) through (6)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly for the 'find and fix anything missing across all 50 states' pass — this file already cited ORC 5747.06(A)(1)-(6) by category name (agricultural labor, domestic service, sub-00/quarter pay, foreign govt/international org service, minors' newspaper delivery, non-cash non-business pay) under withholdingCertificate.withholdingWaiverSectionIII.orc574706Exemption from an earlier pass, but that note was paraphrased, not quoted, and never wired into calc code. Verbatim this pass: (1) "Agricultural labor as defined in division G of section 3121 of Title 26"; (2) "Domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority." Wired via the SAME generic exemptEmploymentCategoryReason() mechanism (src/taxes/state.ts) Alabama already established — only categories (1) and (2) map onto this engine's existing EmploymentCategory enum (agricultural, household); categories (3)-(6) are a dollar threshold, a foreign-service class, a minors-newspaper class, and a non-cash-payment characteristic this engine has no matching shape for — see this file's own knownGaps.

midYearEffectiveDating.rule: The August 1, 2026 table (periodTables above) applies to payroll periods ENDING on or after 2026-08-01. Payroll periods ending BEFORE that date use priorTable2026 below (the October 1, 2025 table, which remained in force through July 31, 2026 — no separate January 2026 table was ever issued).
midYearEffectiveDating.mechanismStatus: CLOSED (Scott: 'fix the gap'): ohioWithholding() (src/taxes/state.ts) now reads thresholdDate directly and selects priorTable2026 for any input.checkDate before it, periodTables on/after — resolved entirely WITHIN Ohio's own dispatch function, not by changing registry.ts's year-only FILE lookup (which was never actually the blocker: both tables already lived in this same OH-2026.json file, loaded together regardless of check date; the missing piece was that nothing inside the state ever chose between them). This is scoped to Ohio specifically for now (the only state in this project with a captured mid-year table so far) rather than built as a cross-state generic mechanism — a second state needing the same shape would be the trigger to generalize it, the same 'reuse when a second consumer appears' convention already used elsewhere in this project.

priorTable2026.$comment: In force for Ohio payroll periods ending 2026-01-01 through 2026-07-31. Same structure as periodTables (per-period exemption, 3 brackets) but different rates — Ohio's brackets dropped between this table and the August 2026 one: 1.775%→1.600% (bottom), 2.990% unchanged (middle), 3.640%→3.400% (top). Exemption-per-period amounts are identical to the August table.

periodTables.$comment: Each table: exemptionPerPeriod (subtracted once per exemption claimed, per period, BEFORE bracket lookup) + 3 brackets (floor, ceiling, base tax at floor, marginal rate). All figures transcribed verbatim from the primary PDF.

annualEquivalent.$comment: Derived (not authoritative — the periodTables above are the source of truth) for human sanity-checking only: floor2 = 500.96*52 ≈ $26,050, floor3 = 1923.08*52 ≈ $100,000, exemption ≈ $650/exemption/year. Notably HB96 removed the historical 0% bracket below $26,050 — the lowest tier is now taxed at 1.6%, not 0%. Do not use these annual figures for calculation; use periodTables directly.

supplementalComment: Flat 2.75% on bonuses/supplemental wages, in effect since 2026-01-01 and UNCHANGED by the August 1 bracket update — confirmed as a separate fact, not assumed to move with the regular-wage tables.
exemptComment: UPGRADED this session from a pure carry-over assumption: ORC 5747.01 (codes.ohio.gov, fetched directly) defines 'Ohio adjusted gross income' as starting from FEDERAL adjusted gross income plus Ohio-specific adjustments — the same federal-AGI-anchor structure Michigan uses. Section 125/401k/403b/457/SIMPLE deferrals are excluded from federal AGI, so by this same anchoring logic they should be excluded from Ohio's base too. ORC 5747.06 (employer withholding duty, also fetched directly) does NOT itself enumerate these exclusions by name — only 6 unrelated categories (agricultural labor, domestic service, etc.). So this is now inferential-from-a-confirmed-statutory-structure, not a bare assumption, but it is still NOT an explicit enumeration the way RAB 1988-27 explicitly names cafeteria plans for Michigan. One tier below Michigan's sourcing; still short of a full pending_verification clear.

withholdingCertificate.$comment: NEW this session: the actual combined IT-4 form, fetched and read directly. As of 2020-12-07 this form ALSO absorbed the standalone IT4NR reciprocity form and IT4MIL/IT MIL SP military forms into one document — meaning the reciprocity mechanism documented separately below (from the older standalone IT4NR) is now actually filed via THIS form's Section III, not a separate one. Also directly relevant to schoolDistrictIncomeTax above: the IT-4 IS the trigger mechanism for school district withholding, not a separate certificate.

source.title: Combined Form IT 4 — Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate (post-2020-12-07 combined version)
source.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and text-extracted directly this session

fields.schoolDistrictOfResidence: Section I — name AND number, directly on the form, cross-referenced against The Finder. This is the actual mechanism by which an employer learns to withhold school district tax at all — ties directly to schoolDistrictIncomeTax above.
fields.exemptionCount: Section II lines 1-4 — a simplified 0/1 checklist (dependent status, marital status) summed into a total exemption count, structurally simpler than Michigan's single free-entry count or federal's multi-step worksheet.
fields.additionalWithholdingPerPay: Section II line 5 — same concept as MI-W4 line 7 and federal Step 4(c). state.ts's applyAdditionalStateWithholding() would read certificate.additionalWithholding and add it to OH_SIT the same as every other state's income-tax method — but see the top-level knownGap below: OH's own income-tax method isn't implemented in incomeTaxLines() yet, so stateIncomeTax() throws for ANY Ohio input before this mechanism is ever reached. Verified directly: calling calculatePaycheck with workState.code:'OH' throws 'Unsupported withholding method "bracket_per_period" for OH'.

withholdingWaiverSectionIII.$comment: Six distinct reasons to claim FULL exemption — richer than a simple 'exempt' checkbox, and this is where the CONFIRMED reciprocity mechanism actually lives now (superseding the standalone IT4NR as the operative form).
withholdingWaiverSectionIII.reciprocalStateResident: Full-year resident of IN/KY/MI/PA/WV — confirms, via this SECOND independent primary source, the same 5-state list already in reciprocity below.
withholdingWaiverSectionIII.nonresidentMilitaryStationedInOhio: Mirror case — military orders don't create OH residency/tax liability.
withholdingWaiverSectionIII.nonresidentMilitarySpouse: Civilian spouse present in Ohio solely due to spouse's military orders (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act territory) — a category with zero representation anywhere else in this dataset.
withholdingWaiverSectionIII.orc574706Exemption: Cites R.C. 5747.06(A)(1) through (6) directly — the exact 6 categories (agricultural labor, domestic service, sub-$300/quarter pay, foreign govt/international org service, minors' newspaper delivery, non-cash non-business pay) already found and documented from that statute earlier this session. Nice closure: the abstract statutory list and the actual taxpayer-facing form now cross-confirm each other.

withholdingCertificate.knownGap: CLOSED: ohioWithholding() now implements the 'bracket_per_period' method (see src/taxes/state.ts) — calculatePaycheck() no longer throws for Ohio input. additionalWithholding now works via the existing generic applyAdditionalStateWithholding() mechanism, verified directly. The military/spouse exemption categories and the school-district-of-residence field remain unreachable, but for a DIFFERENT reason now: those are local/school-district mechanisms this engine doesn't resolve an address against, not a blocked base calculation — see schoolDistrictIncomeTax's own knownGap below, unchanged by this fix.

source.title: Ohio Form IT 4NR — Employee's Statement of Residency in a Reciprocity State (Rev. 5/07), Ohio Department of Taxation
source.verifiedBy: UPGRADED this session from cross_source_confirmed to PRIMARY: downloaded and text-extracted the actual Ohio Dept of Taxation form directly. Quoted from the form itself: 'Ohio employers: You are required to have a copy of this form on file for each employee who is a resident of Indiana, Kentucky, West Virginia, Michigan or Pennsylvania receiving compensation paid in Ohio and who claims exemption from withholding of Ohio income tax under the reciprocal agreements between Ohio and these other states.' This is Ohio's own official reciprocity-exemption form, not a secondary summary of one.

reciprocity.rule: A resident of IN/KY/MI/PA/WV working in Ohio is not subject to Ohio withholding on those wages; income is taxed by the home state instead. CONFIRMED to match the 5-state list already on file — the primary source did not surface any discrepancy.
reciprocity.mechanism: PRIMARY-CONFIRMED general mechanism: the employee files Form IT 4NR with their Ohio employer, declaring under penalty of perjury which reciprocal state they reside in, to claim exemption from Ohio withholding. Must notify the employer within 10 days of any change of residence.
reciprocity.mechanismVariesByState: NOT uniform like Michigan's reciprocity, which is a single symmetric rule. Ohio's exemption mechanism is state-specific: IN uses Form WH-47, KY uses Form 42A809, MI uses Form MI-W4 (all per secondary sources, not re-confirmed against each of those states' own forms this session). PENNSYLVANIA -- DOWNGRADED from 'reported outlier' to 'likely stale/inaccurate claim, not corroborated' (2026-08-21, PA-2026.json's own reciprocity pass): the original claim (PA requires PROOF taxes were paid -- a mailed return + W-2s + statement -- rather than a simple certificate) was re-examined via (1) a direct read of REV-419 itself, which treats all 6 reciprocal states, Ohio included, completely identically with no state-specific carve-out anywhere in its text, and (2) two independent fresh searches this session, both of which describe the Ohio<->PA relationship as an ordinary symmetric IT-4NR/REV-419 certificate exchange with no PA-specific proof requirement mentioned at all. Neither check FOUND the original claim's own source to know what it was actually describing (a genuine possibility: it may have been describing the REFUND process for tax incorrectly withheld, not the prospective withholding-exemption certificate this section governs) -- so this is a reasoned downgrade based on converging evidence, not a definitive primary-source resolution. Still worth a from-scratch verification if it ever matters operationally.
reciprocity.knownGap: CLOSED (Scott: 'fix ohio reciprical tax'): the root cause was never the reciprocity logic itself — reciprocityExemptionReason() already read reciprocalStates correctly — it was that stateIncomeTax() threw before ever reaching it, because Ohio's base income-tax method had no dispatch case. Fixed by implementing ohioWithholding() (see withholdingCertificate.knownGap above). Verified end-to-end directly: an IN resident working in Ohio now gets a genuine $0 OH_SIT line with the correct reciprocity detail message, while an otherwise-identical NY resident (non-reciprocal) still owes full Ohio tax on the same wages — proving the fix doesn't over-apply. The still-open PA-outlier question (proof-of-tax-paid vs. simple certificate) is unrelated to this fix and remains exactly as disclosed above.

interMunicipalCredit.$comment: NEW this session, prompted by realizing 'rate + list of 679 cities' isn't enough for a payroll company — someone who lives in one taxing municipality and works in another needs a defined credit rule, and Ohio actually standardized this by statute (unlike the ad-hoc 'varies by ordinance' picture in the earlier knownGaps note).

source.title: Ohio Revised Code Section 718.121 — Second municipality imposing tax after time period allowed for refund
source.verifiedBy: fetched directly, quoted verbatim: 'the second municipal corporation shall allow a nonrefundable credit, against the tax or withholding the second municipality claims is due with respect to such income or wages, equal to the tax or withholding paid to the first municipal corporation'
source.legislativeHistory: Amended by HB 5 (130th General Assembly), effective 2015-03-23, applicable to municipal taxable years beginning on/after 2016-01-01 — this is the post-uniformity-reform rule, not the pre-2016 patchwork.

interMunicipalCredit.rule: The home (residence) municipality must give a NONREFUNDABLE credit for tax already paid/withheld to the work municipality. If the home rate is LOWER than the work rate, the credit is capped at the home rate (no refund of the excess paid to the work city). If the home rate is HIGHER, the taxpayer owes the difference to the home municipality, plus any penalty/interest for the period it went unpaid. No credit carryforward is permitted.
interMunicipalCredit.practicalImplication: This is the statewide DEFAULT floor, not necessarily the whole story — individual municipalities can be more generous (grant a larger credit) but not less, per HB5's uniformity intent. Not confirmed this session whether any of the 679 municipalities in data/local/OH-municipalities-2026.json actually do grant more than the ORC 718.121 floor; treat the floor as the safe-default assumption.
interMunicipalCredit.knownGap: WIRED (comprehensive-audit pass): ohioLocalTax() in src/taxes/state.ts resolves certificate.residenceCity/workCity against data/local/OH-municipalities-2026.json and applies exactly this credit — home tax minus min(workTax, homeTax), computed at withholding time per the statute's own 'against the tax or withholding' wording, not deferred to the return the way Michigan's return-level credit is. Proven via tests/engine.test.ts, describe('Ohio') > 'municipal income tax (OH_LOCAL)' (both credit directions plus the same-city and no-match cases). Whether any specific municipality grants MORE than this statutory floor is still not checked.

occasionalEntrantExemption.$comment: FOUND AND CLOSED 2026-09-06 on a 'go to every state, fix real bugs not just disclose them' pass — this rule was previously not disclosed ANYWHERE in this file at all, let alone modelled, meaning ohioLocalTax() withheld work-municipality tax starting day one for every nonresident, including someone making a single occasional business trip into a taxing city. That's a real over-withholding bug, the same shape as West Virginia's un-modelled day-count thresholds fixed the same pass.

source.title: Ohio Revised Code Section 718.011 — Withholding requirements for casual entrant employers

occasionalEntrantExemption.rule: A municipality may not require withholding on a nonresident employee's wages if that municipality is NOT the employee's principal place of work AND the employee works there 20 or fewer days in the calendar year. Exceptions where the exemption does NOT apply regardless of day count: (1) the municipality IS the employee's principal place of work; (2) the employee works at a construction site or other temporary worksite reasonably expected to last more than 20 days; (3) the employee resides in that municipality and requests withholding anyway; (4) professional athletes, professional entertainers, or public figures performing services in that capacity. Petroleum refinery workers get a LOWER 12-day threshold instead of 20, with similar exceptions -- not modelled (no worker-industry field exists in this engine to detect that narrow case). 'Small employers' (ORC 718.01) are exempted from this whole mechanism and instead withhold ALL of an employee's wages to the employer's own fixed-location municipality only -- a structurally different withholding regime this engine has no employer-size/employer-fixed-location input to evaluate.
occasionalEntrantExemption.knownGap: WIRED for the core rule and the principal-workplace exception: ohioLocalTax() reads certificate.workCityIsPrincipalWorkplace (default true -- most callers use this engine for an employee's regular duty station, so defaulting to 'exempt' would be the wrong, revenue-losing direction) and certificate.daysWorkedInMunicipality (a caller-supplied cumulative count); the work-city tax line is skipped only when both are supplied and say so. A caller who supplies neither field gets byte-identical output to before this fix. NOT modelled, disclosed rather than guessed at: the professional-athlete/entertainer/public-figure carve-out (no EmploymentCategory value exists for this single narrow case), the 12-day petroleum-refinery-worker variant, the construction/temporary-worksite-over-20-days exception, the resident-requests-withholding-anyway election, and the small-employer alternate regime entirely.

ORC 5747.06(A) names four MORE withholding exemptions this engine cannot represent: (3) any calendar quarter in which cash pay is under $300 — a dollar threshold, not an employment category, and this engine has no per-employer quarterly-cash-wages tracker for Ohio the way it does for household/agricultural FICA coverage elsewhere; (4) services for a foreign government or international organization; (5) newspaper/shopping-news delivery by a worker under 18; (6) non-business services paid in a medium other than cash. None has a matching EmploymentCategory value — reachable only via the generic certificate.exempt + exemptReason route, same boundary as Alabama's own federal-law exemptions.
